title: Serre twist vanishing for projective embeddings of algebraic spaces
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X,Y$ algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Work on their small etale ringed sites, with quasi-coherent modules [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module], module direct images and tensor pullbacks [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], and tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Suppose $Y$ is Noetherian: its etale scheme charts are locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth], $|Y|$ is quasi-compact, and its diagonal is quasi-compact. A module on such a space is coherent if it is quasi-coherent and its pullback to every etale scheme chart is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $n\geq0$ and let $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_Y$ be a closed immersion over $Y$, with structure morphism $f:X\to Y$. Here $\mathbf P^n_Y=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ is the sheaf fibre product [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]; a closed immersion is representable and is a closed immersion of schemes after every scheme test [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The twisting line module $\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_Y}(1)$ is the pullback of the standard projective-space twist over $\mathbf Z$ [def-pc-projective-space-twist], equivalently the line module with the standard transition functions on every etale scheme chart. Put $L=i^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_Y}(1)$. For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$, there is an integer $d_0\geq0$ such that
$$R^qf_*(F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}L^{\otimes d})=0\qquad(d\geq d_0,\ q>0).$$
Higher direct images are right derived functors in all module sheaves, computed by injective resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale atlas $a:U\to Y$ with $U$ affine, using quasi-compactness of $|Y|$. Write $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$. Since every etale scheme chart of $Y$ is locally Noetherian, $U$ is locally Noetherian and, being affine, is a Noetherian scheme. If $Y$ is empty, every module sheaf on it is zero and $d_0=0$ suffices; henceforth the same atlas argument also permits the empty atlas.

source.place: Tag 08AQ, lemma-kill-by-twisting, entire statement; the nonnegative threshold is obtained by increasing the integer threshold to its maximum with zero.

proof.text: Put $X_U=X\times_YU$ and write $b:X_U\to X$, $f_U:X_U\to U$. The fibre-product identity gives $\mathbf P^n_Y\times_YU=\mathbf P^n_U$. By the representable closed-immersion hypothesis in the statement, $i_U:X_U\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_U$ is a closed immersion of schemes: test $i$ on the scheme $\mathbf P^n_U$. Projective space is proper over $U$, and its composite with the closed immersion is proper. Thus $f_U$ is proper, in particular quasi-compact and separated, hence quasi-separated.

source.place: Tag 08AQ, lemma-kill-by-twisting, entire statement; the nonnegative threshold is obtained by increasing the integer threshold to its maximum with zero.

proof.text: Let $F_U$ denote the coherent Zariski module corresponding to $b^*F$ on the scheme $X_U$, and let $L_U=i_U^*\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_U}(1)$. Coherence of $F_U$ is exactly the chartwise coherence required of $F$ in the statement. The etale/Zariski equivalence identifies line modules and commutes with pullback. Since the twisting module is pulled back from $\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$, its further pullback is the same standard twist on $\mathbf P^n_U$. The twist of the statement is the glued module of [def-pc-projective-space-twist] over $\mathbf Z$; the glued-twist identification gives the unique isomorphism $\theta:\mathcal O_{\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}}(1)\to\widetilde{S(1)}$, $S=\mathbf Z[T_0,\dots,T_n]$, with $\theta(e_i)=T_i/1$ and $\theta(T^{\mathrm{gl}}_k)=T_k$ (the index set $\{0,\dots,n\}$ is nonempty). Pulling $\theta$ back along $\rho_U:\mathbf P^n_U\to\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ and then along $i_U$ identifies $L_U$ with $i_U^*\rho_U^*\widetilde{S(1)}$, the module $\mathcal L$ of the projective-ample lemma, and carries the coordinate sections to its sections $s_k$. The projective-ample lemma makes $L_U$ invertible. For each affine open $V\subseteq U$, the closed immersion after restriction is into $\mathbf P^n_V$ by base change; applying that lemma to $V=\operatorname{Spec}B$ says that $L_U|_{f_U^{-1}V}$ is ample. These are precisely the relative ampleness hypotheses needed below.

source.place: Tag 08AQ, lemma-kill-by-twisting, entire statement; the nonnegative threshold is obtained by increasing the integer threshold to its maximum with zero.

proof.text: Apply scheme relative Serre vanishing to the Noetherian scheme $U$, proper morphism $f_U$, coherent quasi-coherent module $F_U$, and invertible module $L_U$ ample over every affine open of $U$. It gives an integer $e$ such that $R^q(f_U)_{\mathrm{Zar},*}(F_U\otimes L_U^{\otimes d})=0$ for every $q>0$ and $d\ge e$. Set $d_0=\max(0,e)$. This is one bound for the entire atlas, independent of $q$.

source.place: Tag 02O1, lemma-kill-by-twisting, applied to the scheme atlas base.

proof.text: Fix $d\ge d_0$ and $q>0$, and put $M_d=F\otimes L^{\otimes d}$. Locally $L$ is free of rank one, so $M_d$ is locally isomorphic to $F$ and is quasi-coherent. The canonical pullback-tensor isomorphism, iterated $d$ times (with the structure module in degree zero), identifies $b^*M_d$ with the etale module of $F_U\otimes L_U^{\otimes d}$. Apply higher-image restriction along $a$ and then the scheme etale/Zariski higher-image comparison for the proper, hence qcqs, morphism $f_U$. They identify $(R^qf_*M_d)|_U$ with the associated etale module of the zero Zariski module obtained in step 4. Therefore $(R^qf_*M_d)|_U=0$.

source.place: Tag 08AQ, lemma-kill-by-twisting, entire statement; the nonnegative threshold is obtained by increasing the integer threshold to its maximum with zero.

proof.text: Write $N=R^qf_*M_d$. For any etale scheme object $T\to Y$, the projection $T\times_YU\to T$ is a surjective etale cover by a scheme, and the restriction of $N$ to it is zero since it factors through $U$. A section in $N(T)$ restricts to zero on this cover, so the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom makes it zero. Thus $N(T)=0$ for every object, and $N=0$. This holds for every $d\ge d_0$ and $q>0$, proving the assertion.
